g.text: HC-SR04 - the ranging engine on both sides
STATUS: GREEN - 4 runs, 4 distances, 199 / 999 / 343 / 1375 mm, every one exact
FIRMWARE SIDE - firmware/sr04_range.pe
PINS
TRIG = pin 6 (SR_TRIG = 0x40), DRIVEN by us
ECHO = pin 5 (SR_ECHO = 0x20), RELEASED
and READ BACK as the pad
TWO SEPARATE PADS, because the host drives one
and listens on the other. Writing a level and
an enable together - the idiom the other acts
use - is impossible here, and the firmware does
not try: dmem[5] is the level and PINOE is the
enable, and they are written on purpose.
TRIGGER
601 clocks
TXPIN = SR_TRIG, PINOE = SR_TRIG, then a
COUNTED delay, then release.
EXACT IN CLOCKS: 4 * SR_TRIG_LEN + 5
, and
SR_TRIG_LEN = 149 makes that
601 clocks
SR_TRIG_LEN IS NOT SR_TRIG.
Both exist and
they are different KINDS of thing:
SR_TRIG = 0x40 the PIN BIT - which pad
SR_TRIG_LEN = 149 the DELAY COUNT - how long
SR_ECHO = 0x20 the pin bit, read back
SR_RECOV_LEN = 117 the sensor's recovery wait
A superseded revision of this figure
printed 4 * SR_TRIG + 4 = 600 clocks, which is
wrong in THREE ways at once - the +4 should be
+5, the count is 601 not 600, and the constant
has the wrong name - and wrong in the way this
family has been repeatedly burned: plausible,
internally consistent, and sitting next to a
formula it did not come from.
The testbench pins 601 as an EQUALITY
, so a
600-clock derivation would have cleared every
datasheet window while failing the act's claim.
RECOVERY
SR_RECOV_LEN = 117
the sensor settles, and only then does
ECHO mean anything. Its ABSENCE was a real
defect once - a program that measures the line
immediately is reading the recovery - and the
wait is now a COUNTED delay like every other
timed interval in the family.
WAIT FOR THE ECHO'S RISING EDGE
spin on the pad until ECHO goes high.
THE ECHO IS CAPTURED, NOT SAMPLED,
which is
what makes this act safe at 4 m: the answer is
the WIDTH of a pulse, and a width does not care
when you looked at it.
MEASURE
t = the echo width in us
the 1 us counter read as a DIFFERENCE,
exactly as in freqmeter.pe and for the same
reason: the clear-on-read flag on port 6 is ONE
BIT, so a poll loop longer than a tick reports
several ticks as one.
THERE IS NO 16-BIT SUBTRACT HERE EITHER,
and for
the same reason as the meter: the counter is RESET
at the echo's rising edge and READ at its falling
edge, so the answer is whatever accumulated.
ONE RESET REMOVES BOTH THE SUBTRACT AND THE
COMPARE, and this machine has no carry flag, so
a subtract is a four-case analysis on bit 7 and a
compare is the same analysis again.
Port 7 is the 4.33 us UART half-bit tick and is
not a microsecond.
CONVERT
THE CONVERSION IS THE ACT,
and it is where
the ISA bites. No multiply, no divide, no carry
flag - only JZ/JNZ.
us = 64q + r
EXACT, because 11q is an integer
So no 16x16 multiply, no division and no
approximation. The plan assumed a multiply;
this identity removes it.
EXACT MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS HERE,
and
conflating them is the defect - see the note
at the foot of this figure.
BANK
the answer
the answer for this run, and dmem[10]
counts the runs.
FOUR runs are banked and all
four match; an earlier revision banked one
and reported the second as an unwritten byte,
which is what the act's last red state was.
STATUS: GREEN
4 runs, 4 distances
image: 387 words loaded (637 NOP-filled)
run 0: echo 1160 us -> 199 mm
run 1: echo 5816 us -> 999 mm
run 2: echo 2000 us -> 343 mm
run 3: echo 8000 us -> 1375 mm
ALL FOUR EXACT.
Run 3 is the interesting one:
8000 = 64 x 125, so r = 0 and the
conversion's truncation is a NO-OP.
NO MUTATION COVERAGE.
mutate_timing_tb.sh has
60 cases and none are sr04, while the
other six acts here are each pinned by
several. The act runs every night and
nothing ever tries to break it - see
the note at the bottom.
SENSOR MODEL - tb/tb_pe_soc_sr04.v
ARM
four targets, one per run, so the firmware
is asked for four measurements and the model
is re-armed between them.
WHY THESE FOUR, and it is not "more is better":
1 160 us a small target
5 816 us exercises the ten-bit path AND the
high byte - an overflow here would be
invisible from the outside, because the
answer would still be a plausible
millimetre figure
2 000 us a mid target
8 000 us 8000 = 64 x 125, so r = 0 and the
conversion's floor() is a NO-OP - the
one input where "exact" means exact with
nothing left over
TRIGGER
detected
each run's trigger is detected and
answered. The old act failed HERE: the model
saw 1 trigger where it had been given 2, and
the trigger was one clock short of the equality
the firmware's own derivation predicted.
CHECKS
per run, the firmware's measured width
and its converted answer are compared with the
model's, and the core is released fresh each
time so the second run cannot inherit the first
run's state.
AND the image length is COUNTED, not assumed:
$readmemh into [0:1023] from a 387-word file
leaves 637 words unwritten and says so only in a
WARNING, so the testbench reads the file's own
length, asks $readmemh for exactly that many
words, and pre-fills the array with 16'hF000.
THE FILL IS CORRECT, NOT A DEFECT:
is NOP and the firmware parks at JMP halt, so
the 637 words are a no-op region behind a program
that never returns there.
"EXACT" MEANS TWO THINGS IN THIS ACT, AND THE AMBIGUITY IS
WORTH A FIGURE.
1. THE IDENTITY IS EXACT.
us*11/64 = 11q + floor(11r/64) introduces no
rounding error at all. That is a statement about the ALGORITHM, and it is the one
the firmware's own header makes.
2. THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT AND THE ANSWER IS TRUNCATED.
199 is floor of it
. So "PASS, an equality"
is exact only AGAINST A TRUNCATING EXPECTATION - and the testbench's "expected 199"
IS that truncation, so the two agree by construction rather than by luck.
3. RUN 3 HAS NO TRUNCATION.
8000 = 64 * 125, so r = 0, floor is the
identity, and 1375 is the whole product. That is the one input where the word is
exact with nothing left over, and it is why four targets beat two: the set now
contains a case that distinguishes senses 1 and 2 BY ITSELF.
A figure or a page that said only "the conversion is exact" was making claim 1 and
being read as claim 2. That is the defect, and the four-run table above is what
makes it impossible to reproduce.
NO MUTATION COVERAGE, and it is a real gap rather than an omission in the
writing.
regress/mutate_timing_tb.sh carries 60 cases across the timing family and
none
of them are sr04; the other six acts in the family are each pinned by several.
The act is wired into run_all.sh and green, so it runs every night - but a suite
that no mutant perturbs cannot distinguish "the testbench would notice" from
"nothing ever tries to break this one".
The identity is strong enough to be worth pinning: a mutation that broke the r = 0
case at 8 000 us, or turned the + 5 in the trigger derivation back into a + 4,
would be caught ONLY because a testbench pins 601 as an equality. Routed rather
than written - regress/ is not this branch's surface.
WHAT THIS FIGURE USED TO SAY, and why it is recorded rather than
deleted.
An earlier revision drew the act as RED - five failing checks, a second measurement
that never ran, an answer of X for an unwritten byte - and printed the trigger as
4 * SR_TRIG + 4 = 600 clocks = 10.000 us. That was MEASURED, not assumed, and it was
wrong in a specific instructive way.
It was wrong about the count, about the +4 versus +5, and about which of two
same-valued constants was meant - and it was wrong in the shape this branch has been
burned by repeatedly: internally consistent, plausible, and derived from something
other than the formula printed a few lines away. The corrected form is above and
the testbench pins 601 as an equality, so the wrong derivation would have cleared
every datasheet window while failing the act's own claim.
the next run
